laws.rule: In Cerro Castillo National Park, CONAF says heat sources and fire are only allowed in places set up for them by the park administration. In March 2026 it reported visitors detected using fire at Campamento Río Turbio who had to leave the park and were cited.

CONAF says introducing polluting substances into water bodies inside protected wild areas is prohibited; washing cookware with detergent in Laguna Cerro Castillo led to infractions in February 2026. No fine amount is stated on the page.

Parque Nacional Isla Guamblin: There is no visitor assistance or public-use infrastructure and access is by sea only. The operator tells visitors to obtain a naval departure clearance (zarpe) from the harbour authority before setting out in a boat of any size. The named unit prohibits fires and other heat sources, pets or exotic animals, leaving enabled trails and removing natural resources. Follow ranger instructions; no region-wide extension is made.

items.text: Parque Nacional Isla Guamblin: CONAF's own unit page prohibits consuming alcoholic drinks. This is the named protected-area condition, not an alcohol ban throughout the region.

Parque Nacional Isla Guamblin: smoking is prohibited in CONAF's published unit conditions. The same page prohibits consuming drugs or hallucinogenic products; no wider possession or prescribing rule is inferred.
